walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermal Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermal Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermal Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Heat travels from the Sun to Earth mainly by:
options: conduction
convection
radiation
all three equally
they have a high specific heat capacity
they have free electrons
their atoms are far apart
they are dense

mcqs.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
options: The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
Heat and temperature are the same thing — both measure how hot something is.
Heat is the energy transferred due to temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.
Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.

mcqs.q: What does specific latent heat measure?
options: The temperature at which a substance melts or boils.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
The energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without changing its temperature.
The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg by 1 degree.
